name: Fluorine
occurrence: Found combined in fluorite and cryolite minerals; too reactive to exist free in nature.
biologicalRelevance: In small controlled amounts it strengthens tooth enamel by converting hydroxyapatite into more acid-resistant fluorapatite — but it's toxic in excess.
notableCharacteristics: The most electronegative element on the periodic table and reactive enough to attack glass, most metals, and even some noble gases under the right conditions.
ncertRelevance: anomalous behaviour of fluorine among halogens
whyHere: Seven valence electrons in the smallest possible second-shell atom means it pulls bonding electrons harder than anything else on the table — the direct reason it tops both the electronegativity and reactivity charts.
didYouKnow: Henri Moissan won the 1906 Nobel Prize partly for isolating fluorine, a task so dangerous that several chemists before him were poisoned or killed trying.
genZNote: Most electronegative element there is. Wants everyone else's electrons and usually gets them.
